## Rules

2. A word means one thing. If it cannot, pick a different word.
3. Vendors are not vocabulary — tools you buy belong in code, never in a

   for a second thing is the defect. Keep one deliberately with
   `monty onto except WORD --where "…" --why "…"`.

skills.name: raea
skills.desc: Make video, motion graphics, games and 3D scenes with raea, the Render Anything Engine, by writing React/TypeScript compositions with raea and rendering them on the GPU with the raea CLI (or playing games live). Use when the user names raea, or wants 3D scenes (Bevy materials, lights, physics, Gaussian splats), 3D placed into footage (matchmove), a playable game, footage cut by its words, cuts timed to a song's beat map, or foley and instruments made locally on the Mac. Also for writing or fixing 3D TSX (Camera3d, Mesh3d, lights, materials, glTF models, post effects, an ECS world), a 3D render or play that looks wrong, extending raea's Bevy SDK, rendered video, captions and motion graphics from code, and frames rendered headlessly.
skills.body: --- name: raea description: Make video, motion graphics, games and 3D scenes with raea, the Render Anything Engine, by writing React/TypeScript compositions with raea and rendering them on the GPU with the raea CLI (or playing games live). Use when the user names raea, or wants 3D scenes (Bevy materials, lights, physics, Gaussian splats), 3D placed into footage (matchmove), a playable game, footage cut by its words, cuts timed to a song's beat map, or foley and instruments made locally on the Mac. Also for writing or fixing 3D TSX (Camera3d, Mesh3d, lights, materials, glTF models, post effects, an ECS world), a 3D render or play that looks wrong, extending raea's Bevy SDK, rendered video, captions and motion graphics from code, and frames rendered headlessly. metadata: raea-tested-against: 0.1.0-rc1 raea-verbs: render play run check init cut song guide skill skills app workspace project spec doctor next library setup gen context brand scene splat blender --- # raea raea renders compositions written in TypeScript and React with a GPU engine built on Bevy. A composition is a function of the frame: give it frame N and it draws frame N. The same file renders to video, plays live as a game, or renders single frames to check. Each step below says where it runs. **HEADLESS**: the `raea` CLI alone, in any shell. **HOST**: needs the raea app running on this machine (its host answers). **PAGE**: needs the person's feed open in the app. **PERSON**: only the person can do it. Every PAGE step says what a headless agent does instead. ## 0. First, every time: which workspace, which project — HEADLESS Before you write, render or generate anything, settle where the work belongs, and keep it all there. Agents most often go wrong by starting to make things first and finding a home for them later, or never. 1. **The workspace.** `raea workspace --json` says which one you're in. The workspaces are the folders under raea.root (`git config --global raea.root`). If you're in none, or not the one this work is for (the studio or client it's for), pick the right one, and ask the person when it isn't clear. `raea workspace init NAME` only when they want a new one. 2. **The project.** `raea workspace --json` lists the workspace's projects and their folders, and `raea project --json` says which one you're in. Pick the one the request belongs to. When none fits, say which project you'd make and make it (`raea project new NAME --client CLIENT`) before any file of the work; ask when it's unclear which one is meant. Projects don't sit inside each other: they're related by their client (who the work is for), as raea cloud tags them, and the raea app gathers a client's projects on its board. Give a new project its client, one `raea workspace --json` already lists under `clients` when the work is for it (the same spelling, never a near-twin); `raea project tag --client CLIENT` gives an existing one its client. 3. **Name it by id.** A project's id is its folder's name, as `raea workspace --json` lists it. Titles repeat and drift, and agents that go by them post to the wrong project; ids don't. So name a project by `WORKSPACE/ID` everywhere (`raea show --project WORKSPACE/ID`, your notes, what you tell the person). When the person pastes a line from the app's Copy reference (a line that reads raea feed item "Hero cut" (i-acp-1) in project "Launch" (launch), workspace "Acme": /path/..., naming no command), it names exactly the thing they mean: that item, in that project. 4. **Say it, then go there.** One line before you start: "Working in WORKSPACE / PROJECT (WORKSPACE/ID)." Then `cd` into the project's folder and read its context (section 3). Everything you make goes in it: compositions in `compositions/`, footage and media in `assets/`, renders in `out/`. Never in the home folder, the Desktop, a temp folder or wherever the shell happened to start. 5. **Plan before you make.** `plan.org` at the top of the project's folder is its to-do list, the one the person sees in the app. Read it, find the task this work is (or add it), and for work of more than one step write the steps as tasks first. Notes from the person (a round of comments, a list of fixes) are planned first too: the work they ask for as tasks in your own words, each linked to the notes it answers, never the notes pasted in. Keep it as you go: mark tasks as you start them, close them with what you made, add what's left. In the app, the plan tools; anywhere else, the file as Org text. [plan.md](plan.md) says how. In the raea app, a chat opened from a project's feed is already in its workspace and project: work there. If the person's request turns out to be for another project partway through, stop, say so, and move to it before going on. ## 1. Install (once) — HEADLESS - macOS (Apple Silicon) or Linux (x86_64): `curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh`. Windows 10 or 11, in PowerShell: `irm https://raea.io/install.ps1 | iex`. Either puts `raea` under `~/.raea`, puts it on your PATH, and adds this skill to `~/.claude/skills`. Run it again to update. `raea help` lists every verb. Linux needs ALSA and fontconfig (`apt install libasound2t64 libfontconfig1` on Ubuntu 24.04). - Another agent: `raea skills install --agent claude|codex|kimi|gemini` puts this skill where that agent reads skills. `--pin quieter` (any move) adds a `/quieter` that loads one move. It also adds raea's hooks to that agent (after a composition is saved, `raea check --quick` runs and hands you what it finds; media opened in the Mac's viewer goes to `raea show` instead, once) and the Blender MCP server; `--no-hooks` and `--no-mcp` leave them out. In Claude Code the skill and hooks also come as a plugin: `/plugin install raea --marketplace shinyobjectz/raea-skills`. - This file's front matter names the raea it shipped with (`version:`). If `raea --version` prints another, read `raea skill` instead: it is this skill as your raea ships it. - From a checkout of the repository: `cargo build --release -p raea-cli`; the binary is `target/release/raea`. - Optional settings live in `~/.raea/env` (`docs/settings.md`). Rendering needs none of them. ## Reference Generated from the code by `tools/skills.sh gen`, so they're current. Read the one you need instead of guessing a flag: - [reference/cli.md](reference/cli.md): every `raea` verb, its flags and where it runs (`raea help` prints the same). - [reference/feed.md](reference/feed.md): the raea app's tools for an agent it launches, and which need its page. - [reference/files.md](reference/files.md): a workspace's and a project's files, what lives in `~/.raea`, and each spec's fields (brief.ts, NAME.script.ts, taste.ts, NAME.parts.ts). - [reference/sdk.md](reference/sdk.md): what each `raea` import gives a composition. - [reference/app.md](reference/app.md): driving the raea app's window over MCP, as a person would (HOST). - [reference/platforms.md](reference/platforms.md): each network the app publishes to: shapes, lengths, file and caption limits, and where its interface covers the frame. ## The guides, by what you're making raea's craft guides travel with this skill: each file under `motion/`, `3d/` and `craft/` is a copy of the guide `raea guide NAME` prints, so either works. Open the router for what you're making; it says which one or two files the task needs. | Making... | Open | |---|---| | anything, built as components that fit together: what each one owns, where each kind gets made (TSX, solids, a generator, Blender, Godot, Rust), materials and shaders as components, shadcn's components on screens, registries | [components.md](components.md) | | a cut of real footage: takes cut by words, faces framed, captions, cuts to a song | [footage.md](footage.md) | | motion graphics and type: cards, stats, logos, end cards | [graphics.md](graphics.md) | | a short product film (a launch, a demo, a brand film) made like a good film of its kind, or one you were handed ("make me one like this") | the video-decompiler skill, installed beside this one by raea's installer and plugin (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | sound: voice, beds, foley, music for picture, the mix | [sound.md](sound.md) | | a 3D scene: lights, materials, models, people, rooms, splats; three.js or React Three Fiber work | [3d.md](3d.md) | | Rust that uses Bevy 0.20 directly: raea's engine and its Bevy SDK, a Bevy game or tool, Bevy code that no longer compiles | the bevy skill, installed beside this one by raea's installer and plugin (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | work inside Blender itself: modeling, UVs, materials and baking, rigging and skinning, shape keys, look-dev, rendering, export | the blender skill, installed beside this one (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | a plain three.js page or scene outside raea | the threejs skill, installed beside this one (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | a game, 2D or 3D | [games.md](games.md) | | an app's interface (web or native) | [apps.md](apps.md) | | generated images, video, sound or meshes | [gen.md](gen.md) | | the export, the share copy, platform specs, posting a deliverable | [delivery.md](delivery.md) | | working with the person in the raea app: the feed, rules, the editor, boards | [collaborate.md](collaborate.md) | | planning the work and keeping its tasks: the project's plan.org, the person's to-do list | [plan.md](plan.md) | | checking a cut against the person's taste and rules, reading their notes on a sound, or teaching their fingerprint | [fingerprint.md](fingerprint.md) | | a story as data: who wants what, what happens and why, each cut's beats, checked, sampled and scored before anything is drawn (raea/story) | [craft/story/router.md](craft/story/router.md) | Across all of them, `craft/`: [craft/ROUTER.md](craft/ROUTER.md) is how to decide what to make (the order of work and reading notes); [craft/floor.md](craft/floor.md) is read right before every edit; `craft/modes/` says what a pitch, an explain, a story, a game or a tool has to do; `craft/verbs/` has one file per move a note asks for; [craft/rubric.md](craft/rubric.md) is how a critique is judged and ranked. `craft/story/` is stories as data: a router, how to write, check, sample and score one, and a page per framework (McKee, the story spine, Storynomics, PAS, Campbell, Vogler, Harmon, Save the Cat, Kishōtenketsu, Propp, Bernays, and the launch film with priors measured on 156 real launch pairs). ## 2. The workspace and its projects — HEADLESS Work lives in a workspace: a git repo under raea.root (`git config --global raea.root`; unset, `~/Studio` where workspaces already are, else `~/Documents/raea`, or `~/raea` when iCloud keeps Documents), one per studio or client, holding projects and the workspace's taste.ts. In the raea app, what you show from a project's folder is a card on its client's board. - `raea workspace init NAME` makes one; `raea workspace adopt DIR` makes an existing folder one. `raea workspace` shows it (`--json` for the projects and their paths). - A project's client is who the work is for (`project.NAME.client` in `.raea/workspace`): `raea project new NAME --client CLIENT`, or `raea project tag [NAME] --client CLIENT` (`--no-client` clears it). Every card `raea show` makes from the folder is filed under it, on its board in the app; a folder with none is its own client, named for it. A project never sits inside another one: two projects for one client share the client. - `raea project new NAME` adds a project: its folder with `brief.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `compositions/`, `components/`, `assets/`, `artifacts/` and `out/`. The workspace's `shared/` has the same folders but `out/`, which any project imports from as `@shared/components/NAME`. A project can live inline or as its own repo (`raea project split NAME`, `raea project join NAME`); both keep its history. - Work in the project's folder. Footage and other media go in `assets/` (`media/` in a project made before the layout), renders in `out/`. ## 3. Read before you make — HEADLESS - `raea context .` in the project prints everything to read first, in order: the person's taste (`~/.raea/taste/taste.ts`; a line there beats any guide's default), the workspace's taste, the brief, the look, the craft floor and each of the brief's modes' guides. Read all of it. In the raea app, `rules_read` lists every rule the work follows, the project's own `taste.ts` first ([collaborate.md](collaborate.md)). - Run it once a session. If it refuses, say so in one line ("raea context failed: its message; reading the brief and taste directly") and read `brief.ts`, any `*.script.ts`, `~/.raea/taste/taste.ts` and the workspace's and the project's `taste.ts` yourself. A `CONTEXT_STALE` line means `raea doctor` finds files from another version: run `raea doctor --fix`. - With no request in hand, `raea next` lists the two or three useful next steps from the brief, the compositions, the renders and their checks. Offer them; never run one unasked. - Standing decisions are taste lines: the person's taste, the workspace's `taste.ts` and the project's `taste.ts` hold what holds for every piece (the delivery spec, the loudness, "always 9:16", "words never cover the action"). A line says it in words and, when something can hold it, names its check: one of raea's forms or checks by name with its values, or a `.ts` check written with `raea/check` (craft/ROUTER.md, step 7). Work to them. Add or change one only when the person says so: `rule_add` in the app, or a line in the project's (or workspace's) `taste.ts`. `raea check PROJECT` runs every line that applies, with raea's floor, and says what waits for a render. - A taste line is not a note. A feed item is one piece of work (a render, a still, a question): the person reviews it once and a note on it is answered by its next version. If the person would say it again on the next piece, it's a taste line; if it's about this piece only, it's a note. When the work needs a decision from the person, ask it in the chat with your best guess (or `feed_propose` what you'd make), rather than burying it in a long reply. - If the brief isn't shaped (no `believe`, no `mode`), shape it before making anything: ask who it's for and the one thing they should believe, or write your best guess and add its field to the brief's `assumed` list. - For a pitch, an explain or a story, plan first: write the deliverable's storyboard as `NAME.script.ts` beside the brief (`export default script({...})` from "raea/brief": scenes of beats, what's on screen and what each scene must land; its fields are in reference/files.md), name it on the deliverable, and add its task to plan.org with the storyboard's feed item on it once posted ([plan.md](plan.md)): their approval closes it. `raea spec NAME.script.ts` checks it. Render nothing until the person approves it (PERSON). - Show a plan as what it will be, in this order: previz (a rough, fast raea render of the blocking, timing and camera: grey shapes, placeholder type, no polish; it is the plan, not the piece, so the gate allows it), else a storyboard (key frames as one `feed_post` look with `files` in order), else the script itself (`feed_post` read with its `NAME.script.ts`: the feed shows it as a screenplay and as an A/V table, timed from each beat's `seconds`). People judge a picture faster than a description. A whiteboard maps how ideas, options and references connect; it isn't the plan. - The person's footage and files: `raea library search "WORDS"` finds them by meaning across the libraries they've indexed (HEADLESS once indexed; adding a folder waits for the person's yes, PERSON). - Right before any edit to a composition, even a one-line change, read the floor: `raea guide craft`. Read `raea guide router` once for the order of work. ## 4. Make an item — HEADLESS One `.tsx` file whose root registers compositions (`raea init` in a footage project writes the files to start from): ```tsx import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, Sequence, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea"; function Card({ text }: { text: string }) { const f = useCurrentFrame(); const opacity = interpolate(f, [0, 12], [0, 1], { extrapolateLeft: "clamp", extrapolateRight: "clamp" }); return {text}; } registerRoot(() => ( ( <> )} /> )); ``` Rules that keep renders right (`raea guide motion` has all ten, under "The core rules"; every file needs these): - **Components first.** List the components the piece needs (each object, surface, effect and card), look in `raea component list` and the workspace's `shared/components/` before writing one, and write what's missing as a component with a fixture that renders it alone. The composition owns the camera, the look and the mix; a component owns only what it draws. [components.md](components.md) says how they fit together and where each kind is made. - **Frame-pure.** Everything that moves reads `useCurrentFrame()`; `useState`, `useEffect` and timers don't animate a render. `Math.random()` is seeded per frame, so seed what should hold still from an index. - **Clamp every interpolate.** Do it unless you mean the line to run on past its ends. - **Cue on words, not on guessed frames.** `word("phrase")` is the frame where it's said, so cues follow the cut. - Footage: `

three.js or React Three Fiber work | [3d.md](3d.md) | | Rust that uses Bevy 0.20 directly: raea's engine and its Bevy SDK, a Bevy game or tool, Bevy code that no longer compiles | the bevy skill, installed beside this one by raea's installer and plugin (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | work inside Blender itself: modeling, UVs, materials and baking, rigging and skinning, shape keys, look-dev, rendering, export | the blender skill, installed beside this one (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | a plain three.js page or scene outside raea | the threejs skill, installed beside this one (not in the plugin directory's edition) | | a game, 2D or 3D | [games.md](games.md) | | an app's interface (web or native) | [apps.md](apps.md) | | generated images, video, sound or meshes | [gen.md](gen.md) | | the export, the share copy, platform specs, posting a deliverable | [delivery.md](delivery.md) | | working with the person in the raea app: the feed, rules, the editor, boards | [collaborate.md](collaborate.md) | | planning the work and keeping its tasks: the project's plan.org, the person's to-do list | [plan.md](plan.md) | | checking a cut against the person's taste and rules, reading their notes on a sound, or teaching their fingerprint | [fingerprint.md](fingerprint.md) | | a story as data: who wants what, what happens and why, each cut's beats, checked, sampled and scored before anything is drawn (raea/story) | [craft/story/router.md](craft/story/router.md) | Across all of them, `craft/`: [craft/ROUTER.md](craft/ROUTER.md) is how to decide what to make (the order of work and reading notes); [craft/floor.md](craft/floor.md) is read right before every edit; `craft/modes/` says what a pitch, an explain, a story, a game or a tool has to do; `craft/verbs/` has one file per move a note asks for; [craft/rubric.md](craft/rubric.md) is how a critique is judged and ranked. `craft/story/` is stories as data: a router, how to write, check, sample and score one, and a page per framework (McKee, the story spine, Storynomics, PAS, Campbell, Vogler, Harmon, Save the Cat, Kishōtenketsu, Propp, Bernays, and the launch film with priors measured on 156 real launch pairs). ## 2. The workspace and its projects — HEADLESS Work lives in a workspace: a git repo under raea.root (`git config --global raea.root`; unset, `~/Studio` where workspaces already are, else `~/Documents/raea`, or `~/raea` when iCloud keeps Documents), one per studio or client, holding projects and the workspace's taste.ts. In the raea app, what you show from a project's folder is a card on its client's board. - `raea workspace init NAME` makes one; `raea workspace adopt DIR` makes an existing folder one. `raea workspace` shows it (`--json` for the projects and their paths). - A project's client is who the work is for (`project.NAME.client` in `.raea/workspace`): `raea project new NAME --client CLIENT`, or `raea project tag [NAME] --client CLIENT` (`--no-client` clears it). Every card `raea show` makes from the folder is filed under it, on its board in the app; a folder with none is its own client, named for it. A project never sits inside another one: two projects for one client share the client. - `raea project new NAME` adds a project: its folder with `brief.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `compositions/`, `components/`, `assets/`, `artifacts/` and `out/`. The workspace's `shared/` has the same folders but `out/`, which any project imports from as `@shared/components/NAME`. A project can live inline or as its own repo (`raea project split NAME`, `raea project join NAME`); both keep its history. - Work in the project's folder. Footage and other media go in `assets/` (`media/` in a project made before the layout), renders in `out/`. ## 3. Read before you make — HEADLESS - `raea context .` in the project prints everything to read first, in order: the person's taste (`~/.raea/taste/taste.ts`; a line there beats any guide's default), the workspace's taste, the brief, the look, the craft floor and each of the brief's modes' guides. Read all of it. In the raea app, `rules_read` lists every rule the work follows, the project's own `taste.ts` first ([collaborate.md](collaborate.md)). - Run it once a session. If it refuses, say so in one line ("raea context failed: its message; reading the brief and taste directly") and read `brief.ts`, any `*.script.ts`, `~/.raea/taste/taste.ts` and the workspace's and the project's `taste.ts` yourself. A `CONTEXT_STALE` line means `raea doctor` finds files from another version: run `raea doctor --fix`. - With no request in hand, `raea next` lists the two or three useful next steps from the brief, the compositions, the renders and their checks. Offer them; never run one unasked. - Standing decisions are taste lines: the person's taste, the workspace's `taste.ts` and the project's `taste.ts` hold what holds for every piece (the delivery spec, the loudness, "always 9:16", "words never cover the action"). A line says it in words and, when something can hold it, names its check: one of raea's forms or checks by name with its values, or a `.ts` check written with `raea/check` (craft/ROUTER.md, step 7). Work to them. Add or change one only when the person says so: `rule_add` in the app, or a line in the project's (or workspace's) `taste.ts`. `raea check PROJECT` runs every line that applies, with raea's floor, and says what waits for a render. - A taste line is not a note. A feed item is one piece of work (a render, a still, a question): the person reviews it once and a note on it is answered by its next version. If the person would say it again on the next piece, it's a taste line; if it's about this piece only, it's a note. When the work needs a decision from the person, ask it in the chat with your best guess (or `feed_propose` what you'd make), rather than burying it in a long reply. - If the brief isn't shaped (no `believe`, no `mode`), shape it before making anything: ask who it's for and the one thing they should believe, or write your best guess and add its field to the brief's `assumed` list. - For a pitch, an explain or a story, plan first: write the deliverable's storyboard as `NAME.script.ts` beside the brief (`export default script({...})` from "raea/brief": scenes of beats, what's on screen and what each scene must land; its fields are in reference/files.md), name it on the deliverable, and add its task to plan.org with the storyboard's feed item on it once posted ([plan.md](plan.md)): their approval closes it. `raea spec NAME.script.ts` checks it. Render nothing until the person approves it (PERSON). - Show a plan as what it will be, in this order: previz (a rough, fast raea render of the blocking, timing and camera: grey shapes, placeholder type, no polish; it is the plan, not the piece, so the gate allows it), else a storyboard (key frames as one `feed_post` look with `files` in order), else the script itself (`feed_post` read with its `NAME.script.ts`: the feed shows it as a screenplay and as an A/V table, timed from each beat's `seconds`). People judge a picture faster than a description. A whiteboard maps how ideas, options and references connect; it isn't the plan. - The person's footage and files: `raea library search "WORDS"` finds them by meaning across the libraries they've indexed (HEADLESS once indexed; adding a folder waits for the person's yes, PERSON). - Right before any edit to a composition, even a one-line change, read the floor: `raea guide craft`. Read `raea guide router` once for the order of work. ## 4. Make an item — HEADLESS One `.tsx` file whose root registers compositions (`raea init` in a footage project writes the files to start from): ```tsx import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, Sequence, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea"; function Card({ text }: { text: string }) { const f = useCurrentFrame(); const opacity = interpolate(f, [0, 12], [0, 1], { extrapolateLeft: "clamp", extrapolateRight: "clamp" }); return {text}; } registerRoot(() => ( ( <> )} /> )); ``` Rules that keep renders right (`raea guide motion` has all ten, under "The core rules"; every file needs these): - **Components first.** List the components the piece needs (each object, surface, effect and card), look in `raea component list` and the workspace's `shared/components/` before writing one, and write what's missing as a component with a fixture that renders it alone. The composition owns the camera, the look and the mix; a component owns only what it draws. [components.md](components.md) says how they fit together and where each kind is made. - **Frame-pure.** Everything that moves reads `useCurrentFrame()`; `useState`, `useEffect` and timers don't animate a render. `Math.random()` is seeded per frame, so seed what should hold still from an index. - **Clamp every interpolate.** Do it unless you mean the line to run on past its ends. - **Cue on words, not on guessed frames.** `word("phrase")` is the frame where it's said, so cues follow the cut. - Footage: `

# Bevy 0.20

raea's engine is Bevy 0.20, the version every skill here is written for. These are Chris Gliddon's bevy-skills, copied
unchanged into `pack/` (UPSTREAM.md says from where). Open the one the task needs; each says which sibling covers the rest.

Start with [pack/bevy/SKILL.md](pack/bevy/SKILL.md) when the task spans several areas. When code written from memory
fails to compile, the migration skills list what changed in each release: renamed types, moved modules, and behaviour
that changed silently (`Tonemapping::None` became a raw passthrough in 0.20; bloom luma became linear in 0.19).

This skill is for Rust. Scenes, films and games made with raea in TypeScript go through the raea skill
(`raea/3d.md`), which maps raea's components onto Bevy's.

## Known traps (found taking a glTF character through Bevy 0.20, 23 November 2026)

- **A glTF's animation needs the loader's own player.** bevy-animation spawns a fresh entity with `AnimationPlayer`
  and `AnimationGraphHandle`; that compiles but never moves a glTF's bones, which are bound to the
  `AnimationPlayer` the loader created. Spawn the scene with `WorldAssetRoot`, observe `On<WorldInstanceReady>`,
  find the `AnimationPlayer` among the scene's descendants, insert the `AnimationGraphHandle` there and play (Bevy's
  own `examples/animation/animated_mesh.rs`).
- **`EXT_meshopt_compression` isn't supported by Bevy 0.20's glTF loader**, and Blender's web export marks it
  required. Export without meshopt for a GLB Bevy loads.
- **Assets outside `assets/`:** set `AssetPlugin { file_path, .. }` (or `unapproved_path_mode`); bevy-assets
  doesn't say so.
- **No Khronos PBR Neutral tonemapper** in 0.20. To match a Blender or three.js look, use AgX in all three.

---
name: bevy-a11y
description: Use when designing or auditing high-standard video-game accessibility in Bevy 0.20, integrating screen readers and focus navigation, supporting adaptive controllers and complete remapping, implementing captions or audio description, checking contrast and motion safety, or building disabled-player test evidence.
license: MIT
compatibility: opencode,claude-code,cursor
metadata:
  tier: "2"

  bevy_version: "0.20"

# Bevy 0.20 — game accessibility

Accessibility is a cross-cutting product requirement. Start during input, UI, audio,
camera, narrative, multiplayer, and save-system design; retrofitting only labels and
captions will not solve inaccessible game mechanics.

## Standard of work

Use all four layers:

1. [Xbox Accessibility Guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/accessibility/guidelines)
   as the public game-specific engineering baseline.
2. [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) criteria, aiming at AAA where they
   transfer meaningfully to game UI/content.
3. Platform-holder requirements and certification guidance for every shipping target.
4. Usability testing with disabled players using their own assistive technology.

WCAG AAA is not a universal native-game certification, and automated checks do not
establish conformance. Record scope, exceptions, devices, test builds, findings, and
remediation evidence. See [requirements](references/requirements.md).

## Ship these foundations first

- Every gameplay and UI action is device-neutral, remappable, conflict-checked,
  persistable, and available through menus without a pointer.
- Input supports hotplug, simultaneous devices, multiple controllers per player,
  unknown controls, adjustable deadzones/sensitivity, and digital analog alternatives.
- Holds, repeated presses, chords, rapid timing, and precision input have toggle,
  timing, or assist alternatives.
- UI has deterministic focus order, visible focus, semantic roles/names/states,
  scalable text/layout, adequate contrast, and no information conveyed only by colour.
- Dialogue and meaningful audio have synchronized closed captions; meaningful visual
  events have narration/audio-description or equivalent cues.
- Camera shake, motion blur, flashes, auto-motion, and other vestibular/photosensitive
  effects have safe defaults or independent controls.
- Accessibility settings are available before first gameplay and remain usable after
  rebinding, language changes, disconnects, and save migration.

## Bevy UI semantics and focus

`DefaultPlugins` includes `InputFocusPlugin`. Add navigation plugins explicitly and
put the accessible name on the same entity as the interactive control:

```rust
use bevy::{
    input_focus::{
        directional_navigation::DirectionalNavigationPlugin,
        tab_navigation::TabNavigationPlugin,
    },
    picking::hover::Hovered,
    prelude::*,
    ui::auto_directional_navigation::AutoDirectionalNavigation,
    ui_widgets::Button,
};

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((
            DefaultPlugins,
            TabNavigationPlugin,
            DirectionalNavigationPlugin,
        ))
        .add_systems(Startup, setup)
        .run();
}

fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.spawn(Camera2d);
    commands.spawn((
        Button,
        Hovered::default(),
        AccessibleLabel::new("Start game"),
        AutoDirectionalNavigation::default(),
        children![Text::new("Start game")],
    ));
}
```

`ui_widgets::Button` requires an AccessKit `Role::Button` node. Read interaction state
as `(&Hovered, Has<Pressed>)`; `ui::Interaction` and `ui::prelude::Button` are deprecated.

Focus, hover, pointer capture, and screen-reader focus are related but not identical.
Test keyboard, D-pad/stick, switch-style scanning, touch, pointer, and a real screen
reader. Use AccessKit nodes for custom widgets and expose changing value/state—not only
a static label. See [screen readers and navigation](references/screen-readers-and-navigation.md).

## Adaptive and accessibility controllers

Adaptive controllers normally arrive through standard gamepad/HID mappings. Do not
gate features on a brand, vendor ID, or a particular device name. Treat every
`Gamepad` entity as capabilities and bindings:

```rust
use bevy::prelude::*;

fn read_gamepads(gamepads: Query<(Entity, &Gamepad)>) {
    for (entity, gamepad) in &gamepads {
        let move_axis = gamepad.left_stick();
        let activate = gamepad.just_pressed(GamepadButton::South);
        let extra = gamepad.just_pressed(GamepadButton::Other(0));
        let _sample = (entity, move_axis, activate, extra);
    }
}
```

With `default-features = false`, native discovery requires Bevy's `bevy_gilrs`
feature, not only `gamepad`. `leafwing-input-manager 0.22` is a compatible optional
action layer, but it does not create accessible settings, UI, persistence, or mechanic
alternatives for you. See [input and adaptive controllers](references/input-and-adaptive-controllers.md).

## Requirements by access need

| Area | Non-negotiable implementation |
|---|---|
| Blind/low vision | semantic UI, full non-pointer navigation, narration/audio description, text scale, strong focus/contrast, non-colour cues |
| Deaf/hard of hearing | closed captions with speaker and meaningful sound cues, visual/haptic equivalents, independent mix controls |
| Motor | full remapping, simultaneous devices, no mandatory holds/mashing/chords, timing/aim/movement assists, pauseability where possible |
| Cognitive/learning | consistent navigation, plain language, objective history, tutorials, adjustable pacing/difficulty, low-distraction modes |
| Speech/communication | no voice-only requirement, accessible text chat, speech-to-text/text-to-speech where communication is core |
| Photosensitive/vestibular | flash safety, reduced motion, shake/FOV/blur controls, no essential parallax/auto-motion |

Read [visual, cognitive, and motion](references/visual-cognitive-motion.md) and
[captions, audio, and communication](references/captions-audio-communication.md).

## Implementation gates

- Run `scripts/audit_input_map.py` on the action manifest before input freezes.
- Run `scripts/check_contrast.py` on every theme/state pair; sample image/video
  backgrounds separately.
- Run `scripts/validate_captions.py` on source and localized VTT/SRT files.
- Execute the manual matrix in [testing and evidence](references/testing-and-evidence.md).
- Do not advertise accessibility feature tags until the shipping build and supported
  input/platform combinations have been verified.

Script formats and CI examples are in [tooling](references/tooling.md).

## Gotchas

- 0.20: `ui::prelude::Button` and `ui::Interaction` are deprecated. Spawn
  `bevy::ui_widgets::Button` and read `(&Hovered, Has<Pressed>)`. Stale output
  queries `Changed<Interaction>`.
- 0.20: `FocusCause` gained `Auto` (focus granted by `AutoFocus`). An exhaustive
  `match` on `Navigated | Pressed` no longer compiles.
- 0.20: `Escape` in a focused `EditableText` clears `InputFocus` and keeps bubbling.
  A dialog cancel observer fires on the same press; test `original_event_target()`
  for two-step behaviour. `EditableText` needs a sibling `TextInput` to be a widget.
- 0.20: pointer events are flat: `On<PointerClick>`, not `On<Pointer<Click>>`;
  the position is `event.pointer.position`.
- 0.20: `GamepadButton::Other(u32)` and `GamepadAxis::Other(u32)` (were `u8`).
- 0.20: `TextFont::default()` size is `FontSize::Rem(1.)`; `Val::Rem` sizes scale
  with the `RemSize` resource, which is the hook for a user text-scale setting.
- 0.19: `InputFocus` fields are private; use `set(entity, cause)`, `get()`, `clear()`.
  `UiWidgetsPlugins` ships in `DefaultPlugins`; tab/directional plugins stay explicit.
- 0.19: `bevy_input_focus` is no longer implied by the `picking` feature; `ui` pulls it in.

## See also

- [`bevy-input-actions`](../bevy-input-actions/SKILL.md) — logical actions,
  remapping, device hot-plug, Steam Deck, and adaptive-controller integration.
- [`bevy-audio`](../bevy-audio/SKILL.md) — captions/cue boundary, category mixes,
  spatial limitations, and browser audio startup.
- [`bevy-ui`](../bevy-ui/SKILL.md) — layout, text, interaction, and focus APIs.
- [`bevy-cargo-features`](../bevy-cargo-features/SKILL.md) — controller and UI backends.
- [`bevy-fluent`](../bevy-fluent/SKILL.md) — localized text and captions.
- [`bevy-cameras`](../bevy-cameras/SKILL.md) — shake, FOV, and viewport controls.
- [`bevy-physics`](../bevy-physics/SKILL.md) — accessible character movement, aim,
  and timing mechanics built over physics.
- [`bevy-testing`](../bevy-testing/SKILL.md) — deterministic checks and capture evidence.
- [`bevy-core-concepts`](../bevy-core-concepts/SKILL.md) — schedule architecture.
- [`bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20`](../bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20/SKILL.md) — deprecated
  `Button`/`Interaction`, flat pointer events, `FocusCause::Auto`.

# Bevy 0.20 — audio

## When to use this skill

- Spawn or control clips/loops through `AudioPlayer` and sink components.
- Build music/ambience transitions, mix categories, ducking, or pause policy.
- Add spatial sources/listeners or define the built-in HRTF/effects boundary.
- Ship audio on browsers or evaluate `bevy_seedling 0.8` (Bevy 0.19 only, see Gotchas).

Use Bevy's built-in entity-based audio for straightforward clips, loops, playback
control, and simple spatial stereo. Add an application mixer policy for categories and
transitions. Move to an audio-graph library only when the measured/design requirement
exceeds that boundary.

## Canonical pattern

```rust
use bevy::{audio::Volume, prelude::*};

#[derive(Component)]
struct Music;

fn start_music(mut commands: Commands, assets: Res<AssetServer>) {
    commands.spawn((
        Name::new("Exploration music"),
        Music,
        AudioPlayer::new(assets.load("audio/exploration.ogg")),
        PlaybackSettings::LOOP.with_volume(Volume::Decibels(-9.0)),
    ));
}

fn mute_music(mut sinks: Query<&mut AudioSink, With<Music>>) {
    for mut sink in &mut sinks {
        sink.mute();
    }
}
```

Bevy inserts `AudioSink` after non-spatial playback begins and `SpatialAudioSink` for
spatial playback. Query the sink for live volume, mute, pause, speed, position, seek,
and stop. Changing `PlaybackSettings` or `GlobalVolume` does not update audio that is
already playing.

`PlaybackSettings::{ONCE, LOOP, DESPAWN, REMOVE}` define completion ownership. An
`ONCE` player cannot simply replay after its sink drains; remove/reinsert the audio
components or spawn a new player. Removing a sink while `AudioPlayer` remains causes
the unchanged source to start again.

## Gotchas

- `PlaybackSettings` and `GlobalVolume` affect initial playback, not existing sinks.
- A sink appears only after playback starts; query it optionally.
- Drained `ONCE` playback is not replayable without replacing audio components.
- Removing a sink while its unchanged player remains restarts the source.
- Built-in spatial audio is stereo panning, not HRTF or a general effects graph.

  (crates.io, 2026-11-03). Adding it to a 0.20 app fails with two `bevy_ecs` versions.

  `On<Add<AudioSink>>` (0.19 output writes `On<Add, AudioSink>`):


  `default-features = false`, add `audio` (and `vorbis`/`mp3`/`flac` as needed) or

## Spatial audio boundary


pose. Configure `SpatialScale` when world units do not match audio distance. Built-in
spatialisation is simple left/right stereo panning: it does not provide HRTF or a full
3D acoustic model.

## Mix groups and transitions

Built-in audio has no general bus/effects graph. Model categories (`Master`, `Music`,
`Sfx`, `Dialogue`, `Ambience`, `Ui`) as application state and tag player entities.

write sinks. Store sliders in decibels or a perceptually useful curve, not a raw linear

time according to pause policy. Do not despawn the old entity until its sink reaches
silence. Preload assets before a latency-critical transition, and define what happens
when a new track is not ready.

## Browser rule

Browsers commonly block audible playback until a user activation. Treat audio unlock
as an explicit app state: let the first intentional input resume/start audio, keep the
request pending if blocked, and present a usable muted/unlock control. Test refresh,
tab background/foreground, device change, and mobile browsers; startup playback is
not evidence that every browser will allow it.

`audio` feature when using Seedling so the two backends/types do not compete. Pin and
test the exact library release and platform.

| Problem | Read |

- Group/master changes update already-playing sinks without losing source gain.

- Exactly one listener exists and scale/pose follow the intended viewpoint.
- Browser audio unlock/failure is visible and recoverable.
- Dialogue has captions and important audio cues have non-audio equivalents.

```rust
        Name::new("Exploration music"),
        Music,
        AudioPlayer::new(assets.load("audio/exploration.ogg")),
        PlaybackSettings::LOOP.with_volume(Volume::Decibels(-9.0)),

    for mut sink in &mut sinks {
        sink.mute();
    }
```

# Bevy 0.20 — Cargo features

## When to use this skill

- Authoring or auditing a Bevy project's `Cargo.toml`.
- Trimming the WASM bundle (the single biggest lever).
- Building a headless server (no rendering, no windowing, no audio).
- Writing a custom renderer that needs Bevy's data types but not its render pipeline.
- Migrating a 0.18 or 0.19 manifest: `ui`, `audio`, `bevy_window` and `custom_cursor` moved collections.

## Canonical patterns

### Top-level collections (what `default` is made of)

```toml
# default = ["2d", "3d", "ui", "audio"]
[dependencies]
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = ["3d", "ui", "audio"] }
# 3D, no bevy_ui (bring your own UI):
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = ["3d", "audio"] }
# 2D, no bevy_audio (e.g. bevy_seedling):
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = ["2d", "ui"] }
```

`2d`, `3d` and `ui` each imply `default_app` + `default_platform` + their `*_bevy_render` stack + `scene` + `picking`. Since 0.19 they imply **neither `ui` nor `audio`**; list those explicitly.

### Mid-level: API without the default renderer

```toml
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = ["3d_api", "bevy_winit", "x11"] }
```

| Collection | Adds | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `common_api` | animation, camera, color, `bevy_curve`, gizmos, image, mesh, shader, material, text, `bevy_window`, hdr, png | base of every `*_api` |
| `2d_api` / `3d_api` | `common_api` + sprite, or + light, mikktspace, ktx2, morph, luts, zstd | custom renderer |
| `ui_api` | `default_app` + `common_api` + `bevy_ui` + `bevy_input_focus` | custom UI renderer |
| `2d_bevy_render` / `3d_bevy_render` / `ui_bevy_render` | `*_api` + `bevy_render` + core pipeline + the stock renderers (`3d` also glTF, PBR, anti-alias, `gltf_animation`) | stock renderer, no `default_platform` |
| `default_app` | `async_executor`, `bevy_asset`, `bevy_log`, `bevy_state`, `reflect_auto_register` | headless |
| `default_platform` | `std`, `bevy_winit`, `bevy_gilrs`, `bevy_clipboard`, `default_font`, `multi_threaded`, `webgl2`, `x11`, `wayland`, `custom_cursor`, `sysinfo_plugin` | desktop windowing |
| `scene` | `bevy_scene` (BSN) + `bevy_world_serialization` (glTF spawning, `WorldAssetRoot`) | any glTF scene |
| `picking` | `bevy_picking` + `mesh_picking` + `sprite_picking` + `ui_picking` | pointer events |

Table derived from `bevy-0.20.1/Cargo.toml`.

### Headless server

```toml
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = [
    "default_app",   # ECS + assets + state + log, no window
    "multi_threaded",
    "serialize",
    "scene",         # only if you spawn glTF / serialize worlds
] }
```

```rust
use bevy::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    // Headless: pair `default-features = false` + "default_app" with
    // `MinimalPlugins`, not `DefaultPlugins` (which needs the render features).
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(MinimalPlugins)
        .add_systems(Update, tick)
        .run();
}

fn tick(time: Res<Time>) {
    let _ = time.delta_secs();
}
```

### Minimal client, opt-in input

```toml
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = [
    "3d_bevy_render", "bevy_winit", "x11",   # or "wayland"; "webgl2"/"webgpu" on web
    "mouse", "keyboard", "gamepad",          # input is opt-in without default_platform
    # "touch", "gestures", "bevy_gilrs" (= gamepad + gilrs backend)
] }
```

### Dev-only extras

```toml
[features]
dev = ["bevy/dev"]   # = debug + bevy_dev_tools + render_dev_tools + file_watcher
```

`render_dev_tools` compiles `RenderDebugOverlayPlugin` into `DefaultPlugins` (disabled until you insert `RenderDebugOverlayKeybindings { enable_keybindings: true, .. }`). Without the feature the overlay is absent; stock `DefaultPlugins` do not include it.

## Feature moves since 0.18

| 0.18 | 0.19 | 0.20 |
|---|---|---|
| `3d`/`2d`/`ui` imply `audio` | `audio` separate, in `default` | same |
| `3d`/`2d` imply `ui` | `ui` separate, in `default` | same |
| `bevy_window` in `default_app` | in `common_api` | same |
| `bevy_input_focus` in `default_app` | in `ui_api` | same |
| `custom_cursor` in `default_app` | in `default_platform` | same; also forwards to `bevy_picking/custom_cursor` (cursor module moved from feathers to picking) |
| `bevy_picking` implied `bevy_input_focus` | no; `ui_picking` does | same |
| `experimental_bevy_feathers` / `experimental_bevy_ui_widgets` | `bevy_feathers` / `bevy_ui_widgets` (`ui` includes widgets) | same |
| `android-game-activity` in default | neither Android activity feature is default; add one | same |
| `bevy_math/curve` (default) | same | gone: enable `bevy/bevy_curve` (in `common_api`) |
| `shader_format_wesl`, `shader_format_glsl` | present | removed: WESL always on, GLSL gone; `shader_format_spirv` stays |
| `compressed_image_saver` = Basis Universal | same | = BCn/ASTC via `ctt`; old behaviour is `compressed_image_saver_universal` |
| — | — | `bevy_shape` is a non-optional dep (no feature); its `serialize` rides on `bevy/serialize` |
| `bevy_transform/bevy_log` | removed; tracing under `trace` | same |
| audio: `vorbis` default; `wav`, `mp3`, `mp4`, `flac`, `aac`, `audio-all-formats` | since 0.19 (rodio 0.22) | same |

## Gotchas

- **`default-features = false` + `3d` drops UI and audio.** Stale 0.18 manifests then hit "no `Node`/`AudioPlayer`". Add `ui` and/or `audio`.
- **`default_app` has no window types.** `Window`, `WindowPlugin` need `bevy_window` (`common_api` or explicit).
- **`bevy_picking` without `ui_picking` gives no UI focus-on-click.** Add `ui` or `ui_picking`.
- **`bevy_math/curve` no longer exists.** `cargo` fails with "feature `curve` not found"; use `bevy/bevy_curve`.
- **`shader_format_wesl`/`shader_format_glsl` fail to resolve** in 0.20. Delete them; port GLSL to WESL.
- **Web texture compression:** use `compressed_image_saver_universal`; the new `compressed_image_saver` output is BCn (desktop) or ASTC (`BEVY_COMPRESSED_IMAGE_SAVER_ASTC=4x4`), not one-file-everywhere.
- **`multi_threaded` implies `std`.** `no_std` targets use `default_no_std`.
- **`trace_tracy` / `trace_chrome`** are separate log sinks; enable one.
- **Asset sources:** `file_watcher` (hot reload), `embedded_watcher`, `http`/`https` (`ureq`), `web_asset_cache`, `asset_processor` are all opt-in.

## See also

- `bevy-wasm-webgpu` — the trimmed WASM manifest and `webgl2`/`webgpu`.
- `bevy-assets` — `file_watcher`, `scene`, `compressed_image_saver*` at runtime.
- `bevy-migration-0-18-to-0-19` and `bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20` — the upstream feature-move notes.

```toml
bevy = { version = "0.20", default-features = false, features = [
    "3d_bevy_render", "bevy_winit", "x11",   # or "wayland"; "webgl2"/"webgpu" on web
    "mouse", "keyboard", "gamepad",          # input is opt-in without default_platform
    # "touch", "gestures", "bevy_gilrs" (= gamepad + gilrs backend)
] }
```

### Dev-only extras

```toml
[features]
dev = ["bevy/dev"]   # = debug + bevy_dev_tools + render_dev_tools + file_watcher
```

`render_dev_tools` compiles `RenderDebugOverlayPlugin` into `DefaultPlugins` (disabled until you insert `RenderDebugOverlayKeybindings { enable_keybindings: true, .. }`). Without the feature the overlay is absent; stock `DefaultPlugins` do not include it.

## Feature moves since 0.18

| 0.18 | 0.19 | 0.20 |
|---|---|---|
| `3d`/`2d`/`ui` imply `audio` | `audio` separate, in `default` | same |
| `3d`/`2d` imply `ui` | `ui` separate, in `default` | same |
| `bevy_window` in `default_app` | in `common_api` | same |
| `bevy_input_focus` in `default_app` | in `ui_api` | same |
| `custom_cursor` in `default_app` | in `default_platform` | same; also forwards to `bevy_picking/custom_cursor` (cursor module moved from feathers to picking) |
| `bevy_picking` implied `bevy_input_focus` | no; `ui_picking` does | same |
| `experimental_bevy_feathers` / `experimental_bevy_ui_widgets` | `bevy_feathers` / `bevy_ui_widgets` (`ui` includes widgets) | same |
| `android-game-activity` in default | neither Android activity feature is default; add one | same |
| `bevy_math/curve` (default) | same | gone: enable `bevy/bevy_curve` (in `common_api`) |
| `shader_format_wesl`, `shader_format_glsl` | present | removed: WESL always on, GLSL gone; `shader_format_spirv` stays |
| `compressed_image_saver` = Basis Universal | same | = BCn/ASTC via `ctt`; old behaviour is `compressed_image_saver_universal` |
| — | — | `bevy_shape` is a non-optional dep (no feature); its `serialize` rides on `bevy/serialize` |
| `bevy_transform/bevy_log` | removed; tracing under `trace` | same |
| audio: `vorbis` default; `wav`, `mp3`, `mp4`, `flac`, `aac`, `audio-all-formats` | since 0.19 (rodio 0.22) | same |

## Gotchas

- **`default-features = false` + `3d` drops UI and audio.** Stale 0.18 manifests then hit "no `Node`/`AudioPlayer`". Add `ui` and/or `audio`.
- **`default_app` has no window types.** `Window`, `WindowPlugin` need `bevy_window` (`common_api` or explicit).
- **`bevy_picking` without `ui_picking` gives no UI focus-on-click.** Add `ui` or `ui_picking`.
- **`bevy_math/curve` no longer exists.** `cargo` fails with "feature `curve` not found"; use `bevy/bevy_curve`.
- **`shader_format_wesl`/`shader_format_glsl` fail to resolve** in 0.20. Delete them; port GLSL to WESL.
- **Web texture compression:** use `compressed_image_saver_universal`; the new `compressed_image_saver` output is BCn (desktop) or ASTC (`BEVY_COMPRESSED_IMAGE_SAVER_ASTC=4x4`), not one-file-everywhere.
- **`multi_threaded` implies `std`.** `no_std` targets use `default_no_std`.
- **`trace_tracy` / `trace_chrome`** are separate log sinks; enable one.
- **Asset sources:** `file_watcher` (hot reload), `embedded_watcher`, `http`/`https` (`ureq`), `web_asset_cache`, `asset_processor` are all opt-in.

## See also

- `bevy-wasm-webgpu` — the trimmed WASM manifest and `webgl2`/`webgpu`.
- `bevy-assets` — `file_watcher`, `scene`, `compressed_image_saver*` at runtime.
- `bevy-migration-0-18-to-0-19` and `bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20` — the upstream feature-move notes.

# Bevy 0.20 — diagnostics and profiling

## When to use this skill

- A frame, render pass, worker pipeline, or upload path needs causal evidence.
- A queue/task system needs stable gauges, counters, latency, and high-water marks.
- Performance claims must pass native, Steam Deck, or browser acceptance budgets.
- Render GPU diagnostics are absent or disagree with CPU traces.

Diagnostics answer “what is happening over time?” Tracing answers “where did this
execution spend time?” Render diagnostics expose pass-level renderer measurements.
Use all three, but do not treat any one of them as proof of a bottleneck.

## Canonical pattern

```rust
use bevy::{
    diagnostic::{
        Diagnostic, DiagnosticPath, Diagnostics, RegisterDiagnostic,
    },
    prelude::*,
};

const REMESH_QUEUE_DEPTH: DiagnosticPath =
    DiagnosticPath::const_new("voxel/remesh_queue_depth");

#[derive(Resource, Default)]
struct RemeshQueue {
    valid_jobs: usize,
}

struct VoxelDiagnosticsPlugin;

impl Plugin for VoxelDiagnosticsPlugin {
    fn build(&self, app: &mut App) {
        app.init_resource::<RemeshQueue>()
            .register_diagnostic(
                Diagnostic::new(REMESH_QUEUE_DEPTH).with_suffix(" sections"),
            )
            .add_systems(Update, record_voxel_diagnostics);
    }
}

fn record_voxel_diagnostics(
    queue: Res<RemeshQueue>,
    mut diagnostics: Diagnostics,
) {
    diagnostics.add_measurement(&REMESH_QUEUE_DEPTH, || queue.valid_jobs as f64);
}
```

Paths are an API: use namespaced, stable names with explicit units in suffixes or
documentation. Register before recording. `DiagnosticsStore` provides latest and
historical/smoothed values for displays and exporters. Measurements are deferred
telemetry, not a same-system synchronisation mechanism.

## Built-in plugins

- `FrameTimeDiagnosticsPlugin`: FPS, frame time, and frame count.
- `EntityCountDiagnosticsPlugin`: live entity count.
- `SystemInformationDiagnosticsPlugin`: process/system CPU and memory on supported
  native targets. It is unavailable/no-op for WASM, iOS, and dynamic-link builds.
- `LogDiagnosticsPlugin`: development output; filter paths and cadence to avoid noise.
- `RenderDiagnosticsPlugin`: CPU/GPU time per recorded render span and pipeline
  statistics where the backend supports them.
- `RenderDebugOverlayPlugin` (0.20): on-screen render debug overlay, in
  `DefaultPlugins` under the `dev` feature (`bevy_dev_tools` + `render_dev_tools`).
  Off until `RenderDebugOverlayKeybindings { enable_keybindings: true, .. }`
  is inserted; F1 cycles mode, F2 cycles opacity.

Add `RenderDiagnosticsPlugin` from `bevy::render::diagnostic`. It creates dynamic
paths shaped like `render/<span>/elapsed_cpu` and, when supported,
`render/<span>/elapsed_gpu` plus invocation/primitive statistics.

## Tracing for causality

Enable a backend in an optimised build:

```text
cargo run --release --features bevy/trace_tracy
cargo run --release --features bevy/trace_chrome
```

`trace_tracy_memory` adds allocation tracking with extra overhead. Add coarse spans
around work whose cause matters:

```rust
use bevy::prelude::*;

fn rebuild_visible_sections() {
    let _span = info_span!("rebuild_visible_sections").entered();
    // measured work
}
```

Avoid high-cardinality span names and per-element spans. Record section/entity IDs as
fields only during targeted captures. Keep a low-overhead diagnostic gauge/counter
for continuous observability and switch on detailed traces for investigation.

## Gotchas and platform truth

- 0.19→0.20: `Render`, `RenderGraph`, and `Core3d` sets order with `chain_weak`.
  A diagnostic-recording render system that relied on an earlier set finishing via
  a channel or atomic needs an explicit `.after(system)`.
- `tracing` is not a direct dependency: write `bevy::log::tracing::field::Empty`.
- Stale output imports `RenderDebugOverlayPlugin` without the `dev` feature; the
  `bevy::dev_tools` module does not exist without `bevy_dev_tools`.

Bevy 0.20 render timestamp queries and pipeline statistics are supported on Vulkan
and DX12. Metal, WebGPU, and WebGL2 expose CPU render timings only through
`RenderDiagnosticsPlugin`. Missing `elapsed_gpu` is an unsupported measurement, not
zero GPU cost. Use vendor/platform GPU profilers where available; RenderDoc is a
graphics debugger, not a performance profiler.

Profile the shipping renderer, resolution, power mode, content, and build profile.
Desktop results do not establish Steam Deck or browser budgets.

## Choose the relevant deep dive

| Problem | Read |
|---|---|
| Metric types, stable paths, diagnostics store, tracing spans | [Diagnostics and tracing](references/diagnostics-and-tracing.md) |
| Render diagnostics, backend limitations, CPU/GPU tool choice | [Render and platform profiling](references/render-and-platform-profiling.md) |
| Acceptance thresholds, replay design, queue/task/upload telemetry | [Budgets and telemetry](references/budgets-and-telemetry.md) |

## Review checklist

- Every number has a type (gauge/counter/histogram), unit, scope, and sampling rule.
- Queue depth excludes obsolete heap entries; latency timestamps use one clock.
- Spans cover queue wait, worker compute, main-thread apply, and render/upload costs.
- Captures are release-like, repeatable, warm, and made on each claimed target.
- Reports include percentiles and worst sustained intervals, not averages alone.
- Unsupported GPU values remain absent and are never converted to zero.
- Instrumentation overhead is measured and disabled/reduced in normal shipping runs.

## See also

- [`bevy-voxel-runtime`](../bevy-voxel-runtime/SKILL.md) — concrete queue, stale-result, and upload metrics.
- [`bevy-rendering`](../bevy-rendering/SKILL.md) — renderer architecture and custom render systems.
- [`bevy-testing`](../bevy-testing/SKILL.md) — deterministic benchmark replays and visual captures.
- [`bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20`](../bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20/SKILL.md) — weak ordering and render-world renames.
- [Bevy diagnostics](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.20.1/bevy/diagnostic/index.html)
- [Bevy render diagnostics](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.20.1/bevy/render/diagnostic/index.html)
- [Bevy 0.20 profiling guide](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/v0.20.1/docs/profiling.md)

# Bevy 0.20 — Localization (es-fluent)

## When to use this skill

- Adding Fluent-based i18n to a Bevy app (`es-fluent-manager-bevy = "0.21"`, which depends on `bevy = "0.20.1"`).
- Defining typed UI messages with `#[derive(EsFluent)]` and `#[derive(BevyFluentText)]`.
- Wrapping a UI text entity with `FluentText<T>` for automatic locale-driven refresh.
- Switching locales at runtime via `LocaleChangeMessage`; confirming via `LocaleChangedMessage`.
- Reading the requested / active locale from `RequestedLanguageId` / `ActiveLanguageId`.

## Canonical pattern — 5-file minimum shape

`Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
bevy                   = "0.20"
es-fluent              = "0.21"   # `derive` is a default feature
es-fluent-manager-bevy = "0.21"   # `macros` + `file_watcher` are default features
unic-langid            = "0.9"
```

`i18n.toml` (crate root, read at compile time):

```toml
fallback_language = "en"
assets_dir = "assets/locales"
```

`src/i18n.rs`:

```rust
es_fluent_manager_bevy::define_i18n_module!();
```

`src/lib.rs` — **message types must live here** (see Gotchas):

```rust
use bevy::prelude::*;
use es_fluent::EsFluent;
use es_fluent_manager_bevy::{
    BevyFluentText, FluentText, I18nPlugin, LocaleChangeMessage, RequestedLanguageId,
};
use unic_langid::langid;

pub mod i18n;

#[derive(BevyFluentText, Clone, EsFluent)]
#[fluent(namespace = "ui")]
pub enum UiMessage { StartGame, Settings, QuitGame }

pub fn build_i18n_plugin() -> I18nPlugin {
    I18nPlugin::with_language(langid!("en"))
}

pub fn setup_ui(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.spawn(Camera2d);
    // FluentText<T> writes translations into the sibling Text (and into child Text entities).
    commands.spawn((FluentText::new(UiMessage::StartGame), Text::new("")));
}

pub fn switch_locale_on_keypress(
    keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>,
    requested: Res<RequestedLanguageId>,
    mut locale_messages: MessageWriter<LocaleChangeMessage>,
) {
    if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::KeyL) {
        let next = if requested.0.to_string() == "en" { langid!("fr") } else { langid!("en") };
        locale_messages.write(LocaleChangeMessage(next));
    }
}
```

`src/main.rs` — thin binary entry point:

```rust
use bevy::prelude::*;
use my_game::{build_i18n_plugin, setup_ui, switch_locale_on_keypress};

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)
        .add_plugins(build_i18n_plugin())
        .add_systems(Startup, setup_ui)
        .add_systems(Update, switch_locale_on_keypress)
        .run();
}
```

Replace `my_game` with your package name (hyphens become underscores). The full
walkthrough — lib-vs-binary rationale, package-name placeholder, pure-binary
workarounds — is in [references/lib-target-layout.md](references/lib-target-layout.md).

## Topics

| Topic | Reference |
|-------|-----------|
| Why types must live in the lib target; `cargo es-fluent generate` invisibility footgun; full layout | [references/lib-target-layout.md](references/lib-target-layout.md) |
| `BevyFluentText` derive vs `FluentText<T>` component; trait bounds; `Text::new("")` | [references/components.md](references/components.md) |
| `LocaleChangeMessage` (request) vs `LocaleChangedMessage` (confirmation); `RequestedLanguageId`; `ActiveLanguageId` | [references/locale-events.md](references/locale-events.md) |
| `i18n.toml` schema, `assets_dir`, `I18nPluginConfig` runtime override | [references/i18n-toml.md](references/i18n-toml.md) |
| `generate`, `watch`, `check`, `clean`, `sync`, `tree`, `fmt`, `status`, `doctor`, `add-locale` | [references/cli.md](references/cli.md) |
| rustc 1.99+ requirement; `rust-toolchain.toml` pin; failure modes on older toolchains | [references/toolchain.md](references/toolchain.md) |

## Gotchas

1. **Version matrix.** `es-fluent-manager-bevy 0.21.x` requires `bevy ^0.20.1` and **rustc 1.99**. `0.20.x` targets Bevy 0.19; `0.18.x` targets Bevy 0.18. Pin the crate line to your Bevy line. See [references/toolchain.md](references/toolchain.md).

2. **Message types were renamed in 0.21.** `LocaleChangeEvent` → `LocaleChangeMessage`, `LocaleChangedEvent` → `LocaleChangedMessage`. Both are Bevy `Message`s: use `MessageWriter` / `MessageReader`, never `EventWriter`. Stale 0.18-era snippets fail with "cannot find type `LocaleChangeEvent`". See [references/locale-events.md](references/locale-events.md).

3. **`cargo es-fluent generate` only sees the lib target.** Message enums declared only in `src/main.rs` are invisible to the CLI and produce empty `.ftl` output with no error. See [references/lib-target-layout.md](references/lib-target-layout.md).

4. **`T` no longer needs `Component` (0.21).** `FluentText<T: FluentMessage>` is the component; registration requires `T: FluentMessage + Send + Sync + 'static`. The 0.18 `ToFluentString + Clone + Component` bound is gone. Keeping `#[derive(Component)]` on `T` is harmless. See [references/components.md](references/components.md).

# Bevy 0.20 — input actions

## When to use this skill

- Gameplay needs device-neutral, persisted, rebindable actions and prompts.
- Controllers can hot-plug/reorder or multiple players/devices share input.
- Mouse capture, focus loss, Steam Deck, or adaptive hardware needs one policy.
- Frame-scoped edges/motion must drive deterministic `FixedUpdate` simulation.

Gameplay consumes logical actions, never raw keys or a hard-coded controller entity.
Translate Bevy's frame input into an action state once, then feed presentation and
fixed simulation from that state.

## Canonical pattern

Bevy updates raw input in `PreUpdate` inside `InputSystems`. Run the translator after
that set so `ButtonInput`, `Gamepad`, input messages, and accumulated mouse motion
represent the current frame:

```rust
use bevy::{input::InputSystems, prelude::*};

fn install_input(app: &mut App) {
    app.init_resource::<ActionBuffer>().add_systems(
        PreUpdate,
        translate_physical_input.after(InputSystems),
    );
}

#[derive(Resource, Default)]
struct ActionBuffer;

fn translate_physical_input(mut _actions: ResMut<ActionBuffer>) {}
```

```text
keyboard / mouse / touch / Gamepad entities / Steam Input
                     |
                     v
        physical bindings + device calibration
                     |
                     v
       active action set/context + conflict policy
                     |
                     v
       frame action state + ordered transition queue
              |                         |
        Update/UI consumers      fixed-tick bridge
```

Use stable serialized action IDs such as `gameplay.jump`, `menu.confirm`, and
`camera.look`. Bindings, labels, prompts, save data, and analytics refer to those IDs;
Rust enum discriminants and catalog order are not persistence contracts.

For an edge whose precise per-device-stream order matters, translate the underlying
keyboard, mouse, or gamepad messages into an ordered queue. A single `just_pressed`
boolean cannot represent two transitions or their order. Held state and filtered axes
may be stored as the latest values.

## Gamepads are entities in Bevy 0.20

```rust
fn inspect_gamepads(gamepads: Query<(Entity, &Gamepad)>) {
    for (entity, gamepad) in &gamepads {
        let move_x = gamepad.get(GamepadAxis::LeftStickX).unwrap_or(0.0);
        let jump_started = gamepad.just_pressed(GamepadButton::South);
        let _sample = (entity, move_x, jump_started);
    }
}
```

Use `GamepadConnectionEvent` for connection changes and `GamepadEvent` when relative
ordering among connection, button, and axis changes matters. Store active-player
assignment separately from bindings. An ECS `Entity` is a live device handle, not a
stable device identity or save-file key.

Configure per-device filtering through its `GamepadSettings` component. Apply an
inner deadzone, optional outer calibration, response curve, and final clamp once.
Do not apply a second hidden deadzone in gameplay code.

## Gotchas: frame input is not fixed-tick input

Raw input is frame-scoped; fixed simulation may run zero, one, or many ticks in that
frame. Therefore:

- retain ordered press/release transitions until a fixed tick consumes them;
- accumulate relative motion until that same tick;
- drain transitions and relative motion once, on the first available tick;
- copy held buttons and absolute axes to every fixed tick;
- never re-read `just_pressed` or `AccumulatedMouseMotion` independently in each
  `FixedUpdate` iteration.

For rollback/network simulation, convert the bridge output into an explicit command
frame keyed by simulation tick and retain it for replay.

### Mouse capture and focus

Capture through the primary window's `CursorOptions`: hide the cursor and request
`CursorGrabMode::Locked` when gameplay owns look input. On focus loss, pause or
neutralise gameplay input, release capture, synthesize required action releases, and
clear relative motion. Reacquire only from an intentional user gesture; never trap
the pointer merely because focus returned.

Keyboard state is released by Bevy on focus loss, while gamepad state is independent
of window focus. Your action layer still needs one policy that prevents stuck or
unexpected gameplay actions.

### Version traps

- 0.20: `GamepadButton::Other(u32)` / `GamepadAxis::Other(u32)` (were `u8`).
- 0.20: UI pointer events are flat. Write `On<PointerPress>` with
  `event.pointer.position`, not `On<Pointer<Press>>` with `pointer_location`.
- 0.20: `EntityCursor`, `DefaultCursor`, `CursorIconPlugin` live in
  `bevy::picking::cursor`; the `custom_cursor` feature belongs to `bevy_picking`.
  `CursorOptions` (grab mode, visibility) is still a window-entity component:
  `Single<&mut CursorOptions, With<PrimaryWindow>>`.
- 0.20: `chain_weak` relaxed several built-in schedules; `PreUpdate`/`InputSystems`
  is not one of them, and `.after(InputSystems)` is still a strict edge.
- 0.19: `InputFocus` fields are private (`set`/`get`/`clear`), and
  `bevy_input_focus` is no longer implied by the `picking` feature.
- 0.18+: connection changes are messages: `MessageReader<GamepadConnectionEvent>`,
  not `EventReader`.

## Choose the relevant deep dive

| Problem | Read |
|---|---|
| Stable actions, binding grammar, contexts, rebinding and conflicts | [Actions and rebinding](references/action-model-and-rebinding.md) |
| Device assignment, hot-plug, deadzones, Steam Deck and adaptive hardware | [Gamepads and platforms](references/gamepads-and-platforms.md) |
| Edge queues, mouse accumulation, zero/multiple fixed ticks, rollback | [Fixed-step buffering](references/fixed-step-buffering.md) |

## Review checklist

- Every gameplay operation is bindable through a named action, including menu and
  accessibility paths; essential actions offer alternatives to chords/holds.
- Prompts resolve the active binding and device glyph rather than naming a key.
- Disconnecting one controller does not silently transfer its player to another.
- Press+release between two fixed ticks is delivered, exactly once, in order.
- Mouse motion is neither lost on a zero-tick frame nor multiplied on catch-up ticks.
- Focus loss cannot leave a held action or captured pointer stuck.
- Steam Deck and adaptive-controller testing uses real hardware and saved rebinding.

## See also

- [`bevy-a11y`](../bevy-a11y/SKILL.md) — action accessibility and controller acceptance criteria.
- [`bevy-core-concepts`](../bevy-core-concepts/SKILL.md) — `PreUpdate`, `Update`, and `FixedUpdate`.
- [`bevy-testing`](../bevy-testing/SKILL.md) — deterministic fixed-step input tests.
- [`bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20`](../bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20/SKILL.md) — cursor module move, flat pointer events.
- [Bevy gamepad module](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.20.1/bevy/input/gamepad/index.html)

# Bevy 0.18 → 0.19 — Migration cheat sheet

**Released 2026-06-18.** Apply top-down — earlier items break later builds if skipped. Going all the way to 0.20? Finish this sheet, then `bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20`.

## When to use this skill

- Compiler errors after a `bevy = "0.18"` → `bevy = "0.19"` bump.
- LLM emits 0.18-era text/font/scene API names from training data.
- A `#[derive(Resource)]` type suddenly behaves like a component.
- A third-party crate (`bevy_capture`, etc.) hasn't shipped 0.19 yet.

## The renames you'll hit first

### Text layout: drop the `new_with_` prefix

```rust
// 0.19
TextLayout::justify(Justify::Left)   // was new_with_justify
TextLayout::linebreak(/* … */)       // was new_with_linebreak
TextLayout::no_wrap()                // was new_with_no_wrap
```

### `TextFont` fields changed type: `FontSource` + `FontSize`

```rust
// 0.19 — font is FontSource (handle OR family), font_size is FontSize
TextFont {
    font: asset_server.load("fonts/FiraSans-Bold.ttf").into(), // Handle → FontSource via .into()
    font_size: FontSize::Px(24.0),                             // f32 → FontSize::Px / ::Vh / ::Rem
    ..default()
}
// Select by family (needs the `bevy/system_font_discovery` feature for installed fonts):
TextFont { font: FontSource::family("Fira Sans"), ..default() }
```

0.19 swapped the cosmic-text layout backend for **Parley**, which does font fallback
automatically via `fontique`. The old "insert a `DefaultFontHandle` so `..default()`
entities inherit a font" trick is obsolete — see [references/text-and-fonts.md](references/text-and-fonts.md).

### Scene serialization crate was renamed (silent wrong-crate trap)

`bevy_scene` is **reused** for the new BSN system. Classic `DynamicScene` round-trip
serialization moved to **`bevy_world_serialization`**:

```rust
// 0.18  → 0.19
// bevy_scene::DynamicScene          → bevy_world_serialization::DynamicWorld
// bevy::scene::SceneRoot            → bevy::world_serialization::WorldAssetRoot
// DynamicSceneBuilder               → DynamicWorldBuilder
// SceneSpawner                      → WorldInstanceSpawner
```

glTF scene spawning still uses the old (now `world_serialization`) system. Full table:
[references/scene-serialization.md](references/scene-serialization.md).

### Resources are now Components (mostly a mental-model change)

`Res<T>`, `ResMut<T>`, `#[derive(Resource)]`, and `insert_resource` **all still work.**
The narrow breakages:

```rust
// ILLEGAL in 0.19 — a type can no longer be both:
#[derive(Component, Resource)] struct Health(u32);
```

Plus: a resource type now also matches `Query<&T>`, and inserting it as a *component*
can despawn other copies. Non-send resource methods were renamed (deprecated, not removed):

```rust
world.init_non_send::<T>();    // was init_non_send_resource
world.get_non_send::<T>();     // was get_non_send_resource
```

Details + the query/despawn footgun: [references/resources-as-components.md](references/resources-as-components.md).

## Cargo feature implications tightened

```toml
# 0.19: audio is NO LONGER implied by 2d / 3d / ui — add it explicitly:
bevy = { version = "0.19", features = ["3d", "bevy_audio", "vorbis"] }
# ui is NO LONGER implied by 2d / 3d either — add "ui" if you build UI.
```

## Feathers UI stabilized

`experimental_` dropped. `FeathersPlugin` → `FeathersCorePlugin`, and widget components
lost their `Core` prefix (`CoreScrollbarThumb` → `ScrollbarThumb`,
`CoreSliderDragState` → `SliderDragState`, etc.). Only relevant if you use Feathers.

## Third-party crates lag the release

`bevy_capture` (the crate behind `bevy-capture`) tracks Bevy and may not have a 0.19
release yet — **verify a 0.19-compatible version exists before bumping.** When it does,
`EasyScreenRecordPlugin` gained a required `output_dir: Option<PathBuf>` field
(only breaks manual struct construction; `..default()` is fine).

## Gotchas

- **`#[reflect(Resource)]`** reflection access now also needs `ReflectComponent` in some paths.
- **`TextFont::default().font` is a `FontSource`, not a `Handle<Font>`** — code that read it as a handle won't compile.
- **System font discovery** needs the `bevy/system_font_discovery` feature; on Linux also `libfontconfig1-dev`.
- The fallback setters (`set_serif_family`, etc.) now return `Result` — and you mostly shouldn't need them under Parley.

## See also

- `bevy-migration-0-19-to-0-20` — the next release's catalogue.
- `bevy-migration-0-17-to-0-18` — the previous release's rename catalogue.
- `bevy-ui` — `TextFont`/`FontSize`/`FontSource` in everyday UI code.
- `bevy-cargo-features` — feature-implication table and renames.
- `bevy-ecs-components` — the Component model the new Resource subtrait plugs into.
